nodes.description: Inducible deletion of gammaENaC in the adult nephron produces salt wasting with severe hyperkalemia that, unlike alpha or beta subunit deletion, is not corrected by a high-sodium low-potassium diet but is prevented by a potassium-free diet.

Airway ENaC absorbs sodium and liquid from the airway surface. Patients with systemic PHA1 have no airway sodium absorption, more than double the normal airway surface liquid volume, and recurrent chest congestion, coughing and wheezing in early childhood. These data come from cohorts with ENaC subunit mutations generally. gammaENaC-null mice clear neonatal lung liquid more slowly than controls but reach nearly normal lung water, so the gamma subunit facilitates but is not essential for perinatal lung liquid clearance.

nodes.description: Biallelic splice-site, frameshift, deletion or missense SCNN1G variants remove or impair the ENaC gamma subunit. The 318-1G>A allele produces two aberrant transcripts, one predicting a protein truncated from 649 to 134 amino acids. The hypomorphic p.Gly532Ser allele reduces but does not abolish channel expression and activity, which matches its milder phenotype.

nodes.description: Lowering dietary potassium reduces urinary sodium loss and restores volume. The proposed explanation is that low plasma potassium activates WNK signalling in the distal convoluted tubule, so the thiazide-sensitive NaCl cotransporter and pendrin take over sodium reabsorption from the non-functional ENaC. In nephron-specific gammaENaC knockout mice only removal of dietary potassium prevented hyperkalemia and weight loss.

evidence.reference_title: Dietary potassium restriction attenuates urinary sodium wasting in the generalized form of pseudohypoaldosteronism type 1.
evidence.snippet: reduction of daily dietary potassium intake from 40 to 20 mEq induced rapid restoration of volume depletion, as evidenced by weight gain, elevation of the serum sodium level from 133 to 141 mEq/L, decreased urinary sodium excretion, and normalized renin activity.

evidence.reference_title: Dietary potassium restriction attenuates urinary sodium wasting in the generalized form of pseudohypoaldosteronism type 1.
evidence.snippet: Thus, potassium restriction causes NCC and pendrin to compensate for the non-functional ENaC in the collecting duct.

evidence.snippet: However, when K+ was eliminated from the diet at the time that γENaC was deleted, plasma K+ concentration and NCC activity remained normal, and progressive weight loss was prevented.

nodes.description: In principal cells of the aldosterone-sensitive distal nephron and collecting duct, ENaC provides the rate-limiting apical step of sodium reabsorption. Without a functional gamma subunit, aldosterone cannot drive sodium reabsorption, producing end-organ mineralocorticoid resistance and urinary salt wasting.
